system.name: Stochastic Control Guidance (SCG)
system.one_liner: A training-free, plug-and-play guidance method that makes pretrained diffusion models follow non-differentiable rules by sampling candidates at each step and keeping the most rule-compliant.

content.variant_note: an overview chain plus a wedge zoom into one sampling step that branches into three candidates, scores each with the rules and keeps the best
content.argues: Rules that cannot be differentiated can still guide a pretrained diffusion model: at every step sample several next states, score their clean-sample estimates with the rules, and keep the best.
content.subject: A pretrained diffusion chain guided by rule programs, and a zoom into one sampling step that branches into three candidates, scores them with the rules and keeps the best.

elements.name: Rule Programs
elements.role: symbolic rules written as code, here a chord-extraction function, that define the target
elements.drawn_as: rounded white box with a bold title and a monospace listing: def find_chords(notes): ... return [I, IV, V, ...]

elements.name: Pretrained Diffusion Model
elements.role: the unchanged pretrained model that denoises from x_T to x_0 and receives rule guidance at every step
elements.drawn_as: rounded white box with a bold title holding a chain of state strips and arrows

elements.name: x_T, x_{T-1}, ..., x_0
elements.role: the states of the sampling chain from noise to a clean sample
elements.drawn_as: row of light-blue four-cell strips joined by arrows, an ellipsis in the middle

elements.name: Stochastic Control Guidance (SCG)
elements.role: the guidance performed at one sampling step, shown enlarged
elements.drawn_as: large rounded box under the top row with a bold title, reached by a translucent light-blue wedge

elements.name: x_t
elements.role: the current noisy state at step t
elements.drawn_as: bold x with subscript t beside a light-blue four-cell strip, at the left of the zoom box

elements.name: x^1_{t-1}, x^2_{t-1}, x^3_{t-1}
elements.role: several realizations of the next step, sampled from x_t
elements.drawn_as: three strips in rows, fanned out from x_t by arrows; rows 1 and 3 light blue, row 2 orange

elements.name: x-hat^1_0, x-hat^2_0, x-hat^3_0
elements.role: the clean sample estimated from each candidate
elements.drawn_as: bold x with hat, subscript 0 and superscript index, each followed by a score thumbnail

elements.name: Rules
elements.role: evaluates the rule function on each clean-sample estimate (forward evaluation only)
elements.drawn_as: tall rounded white box with bold label, three arrows in and three out

elements.name: loss bars with l(y, rule(x-hat^i_0))
elements.role: loss of each candidate against the target y; the shortest bar belongs to the best candidate
elements.drawn_as: three horizontal bars on a vertical axis line, two solid blue, the short middle one light orange; formula label above

elements.name: smiley face
elements.role: marks the candidate with the lowest loss as the chosen one
elements.drawn_as: outline smiley beside the short orange bar, followed by an arrow

elements.name: x^2_{t-1} (selected)
elements.role: the chosen next state that continues the sampling chain
elements.drawn_as: bold x with superscript 2 and subscript t-1 beside an orange four-cell strip at the right of the zoom box

lessons.what_to_learn: Zoom from a short overview chain into one step with a translucent wedge; in the zoom fan one state into parallel candidate rows through the same checker, show the comparison as a bar glyph, and mark the winner with a colour switch and a smiley that carries on to the next state.
lessons.suits: Sampling-time or inference-time algorithms (best-of-N, guidance, search, rejection) that repeat a branch, score and select step inside a longer generative chain.

evidence: we generate multiple realizations at each sampling step, and select the one that best follows the target (Figure 1)
we sample several realizations of the next step, and select the one yielding the most rule-compliant clean sample

summary: The paper proposes Stochastic Control Guidance (SCG), a training-free, plug-and-play way to guide pretrained diffusion models for symbolic music with non-differentiable rules such as chord progressions, needing only forward evaluation of the rule function. Figure 1 gives the overview in two bands. At the top, a rounded box of rule code (find_chords) sits beside a Pretrained Diffusion Model drawn as a chain of blue four-cell state strips from x_T to x_0, ending in a sheet-music rendering, with a line from the rules feeding every step. A translucent wedge zooms into SCG: x_t branches into three candidates x_{t-1}, each turned into a clean-sample score, checked by a Rules box and compared as three loss bars; the shortest (orange, with a smiley) becomes the next state.
summary_zh: 论文提出随机控制引导（SCG），无需训练即可让预训练扩散模型遵循不可微的音乐规则。图1上方是规则程序与扩散链，下方放大到SCG：x_t分出三个候选，经Rules评分，损失最短者（橙色笑脸）成为下一状态。
notes: Prior kinds kept in a different order: the zoom opens a procedure (branch, score, select), not a learned model, so stage-pipeline is primary and model-anatomy stays as secondary for the unrolled diffusion chain and the overview-plus-zoom layout. The digest lists 4 different bitmaps (3 JPEG, 1 PNG); which of them are the score thumbnails and which one the smiley was judged from the preview, not from the SVG.
